text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A new jump in stock prices; the official 60-share index reaches the highest level in five months.
- Opposition deputies condemn U.S. attacks on Iraq, call for release of detainees and welcome early elections under a new electoral law.
- Light tremor hits the Red Sea port city of Aqaba.
- Supply Ministry seizes forged ration cards in Zarqa.
- Arab-Israeli Knesset deputy Darawshah thanks King Hussein and Crown Prince Hassan for accepting "1948 Palestinians" (Arab Israelis) in Jordanian universities.
- Central Bank issues 15 million dinars' worth of certificates of deposit and accepts repurchase accords.
- Trade and industry minister's visit to Tehran for meeting of the two countries' joint economic committee has been delayed.
- Parliamentary public liberties committee calls on the government to release detainees.
- Supply Minister says strategic stockpile of grains will help stabilise prices.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says Kuwait is entitled to defend itself in face of Iraqi threats.
- Jordan and Britain conduct joint exercises.
